flagged.title: Context: Neurodiversity & Narration
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly tells students that neurodiversity context is 'prime AO4 material' and must be brought into the exam, when context is completely unassessed on this question and AO4 assesses writing accuracy.

mark_affecting.quote: This is prime AO4 material, folks. When Mark Haddon published the novel back in 2003, public understanding of autism was still largely shaped by what's called the deficit model...

mark_affecting.video_says: This is the exact context you need to be bringing into your exam.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: Context is not assessed on this question, so use the theatrical background (2012, National Theatre, Stephens's adaptation) to sharpen your reading rather than to win marks.

flagged.title: Truth & Resolution
flagged.reason: The video refers to Christopher's achievement as an 'A*' at 01:32, teaching an incorrect exam outcome that would cause students to be marked wrong on questions in this lesson.

mark_affecting.quote: Christopher's A* isn't just some private, quiet victory.

flagged.title: Key Themes & Exam Technique
flagged.reason: The video repeatedly labels context as 'AO4 context' and instructs students to use stagecraft and theatrical background to earn AO4 marks, whereas AO4 is strictly spelling, punctuation, and grammar (SPaG), and context (AO3) is not awarded marks in this component.

mark_affecting.video_says: To secure those assessment objective 4 or AO4 context marks, we need the mortar that holds your entire analytical essay together... To really grab those top-tier AO4 marks, you've got to talk about stagecraft.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: Context is AO3 in the assessment objectives. Note that the post-1914 prose and drama question is assessed on AO1, AO2 and AO4 only, so context earns no marks of its own here... Protect the five AO4 marks by writing accurately and ambitiously: varied sentence structures, precise vocabulary, correct spelling and punctuation.
